policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: The clause is rendered 'and the goings out thereof shall be southward of Kadesh-barnea', with no ASV note attached. English verb number here follows its own plural subject 'goings out' (plural תוצאתיו), so it reflects the noun, not the Hebrew verb: the plural qere וְהָיוּ and the singular ketiv והיה both yield exactly this English, since Hebrew freely admits a singular verb before a plural subject. Nothing in the ASV wording, italics, or notes distinguishes the two; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
